note: Rewritten from the original description of Emerson 1925 (English); the original published the species as Rhinotermes (Rhinotermes) tenebrosus, later placed in Dolichorhinotermes. The minor-soldier measurements abbreviate decimals in the original (e.g. .64) and are given here as 0.64; the distance of the lower margin of the compound eye in the alate is worded in the original as "about ½ their diameter".

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, densely covered with many long setae, broadly oval. The antennae are yellow, with 20 segments, segment 2 as long as segment 3, segment 3 slightly larger than segment 4. The compound eyes are of medium size, their lower margin about 1/2 of the compound eye diameter from the lower margin of the head. The ocelli are small, slightly larger than the fontanelle, their distance from the compound eye slightly greater than their own length. The tip of the clypeus is yellow, projecting, rounded at the tip. The pronotum is dark brown, its margins densely covered with many long setae; much narrower than the head, the sides rounded, the posterior margin slightly concave; the legs are yellow. The wings are dark smoky, without a fringe; the media and cubitus are indistinct and merge with irregular thickened areas into a reticulate pattern. The abdominal tergites are dark brown and densely covered with setae; the abdominal sternites are brown and contrast markedly with the yellow thorax and legs. Measurements: length with wings 8.53—8.82 mm, length without wings 5.00—5.88 mm, head length 1.29—1.35 mm, head width 1.18—1.24 mm, antennal length 2.35—2.41 mm, diameter of the compound eye 0.24 mm, pronotum length 0.59 mm and width 0.93—1.00 mm, hind tibia 1.45 mm, forewing length 5.88—6.06 mm and width 1.82 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major soldier: head brown, densely covered with erect setae; longer than wide, slightly wider posteriorly than anteriorly, the posterior margin rounded. The antennae are pale, with 16 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 2 or segment 4. The labrum is narrow and long, reaching at least 2/3 of the length of the mandibles, rounded at the tip. The mandibles are large and stout: the left mandible has 2 large, well-separated teeth, with a further inconspicuous minute third tooth near the base, the first tooth much larger than the second; the right mandible has 2 large teeth, with a further distinct small third tooth near the base, the space between the first and second teeth rounded, the second tooth much larger than the first. The pronotum is brown and densely covered with setae; the legs are pale; the abdominal tergites are densely covered with setae. Measurements: body length 3.70—5.80 mm, head length 1.76—2.03 mm, head length (to the tip of the labrum) 1.65—1.73 mm, head width 1.10—1.12 mm, antennal length 1.71—1.82 mm, pronotum length 0.35—0.38 mm and width 0.64—0.71 mm, hind tibia 1.00—1.12 mm, length of the left mandible 0.95—1.00 mm.
Minor soldier: head, thorax and abdominal tergites brown and densely covered with setae; legs and antennae pale. The head is widest behind the antennae, the sides narrowing posteriorly, the posterior margin rounded. The labrum is very slender and forked at the tip; the mandibles are reduced. The antennae have 15—16 segments. Measurements: body length 3.43—3.80 mm, head length 1.47—1.50 mm, head width 0.64—0.70 mm, antennal length 1.71—1.76 mm, labrum length 0.75—0.76 mm, hind tibia 0.75—0.82 mm, pronotum length 0.32—0.35 mm and width 0.42—0.53 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Differs from Dolichorhinotermes longilabius in the abdominal sternites being dark instead of yellow and in the pronotum being smaller relative to the head, with the T-shaped mark on the pronotum less conspicuous than in that species. The mandibular dentition of the major soldier also differs, and the body colour is brown instead of yellow. The type locality is Kartabo, British Guiana; the holotype is a major soldier and the morphotype an alate; the description is based on specimens of all castes from 6 different colonies.
